An engraved gold-foil seal: a guilloché border, line-engraved shading and metallic gold, with the same meaning built into every element and every count.

Symbolism

Meaning, in numbers

13

Rays of palay

Kindergarten plus Grades 1 to 12: every level of the integrated K–12 school rises from the same sun. Drawn as grains of palay for the harvest and the gold of Rosario.

2

Mountain peaks

The elementary and secondary departments: two schools that became one integrated school.

1

Book-bridge

An open book is the deck of a highland hanging bridge between the two peaks. Education joins the levels and carries learners across to opportunity: together we bridge.

4

Rice terraces

The four DepEd core values, Maka-Diyos, Maka-tao, Makakalikasan and Makabansa, built step by step like terraces in the valley the school serves.

3

Stars

Learners, teachers, and parents with the community: the three who succeed together.

13

Grains on each stalk

Two stalks of palay grow up out of the terraces, each carrying thirteen grains: the same thirteen levels as the rays. What the light of learning gives, the community harvests.

Construction: 13 rays at 12.5° intervals across 150°; stars at 17° intervals around the sun; concentric rings at r 170 · 182.5 · 185.5 · 222 · 233 · 244.5.
Anatomy of the Seal

Built like an heirloom

The rising sun

A young school, founded 2012, still rising. Its face is engraved in fine rings, like a struck medal.

The woven ring

A Cordillera-style diamond weave encircles the scene: the school’s Indigenous learners and heritage hold everything together.

The guilloché border

The interlaced lines found on banknotes and diplomas: a seal made to be trusted, and hard to copy.

20 · 12

The founding year flanks the seal at left and right, where the name and the motto meet.

Logo Family

One seal, three sizes of voice

Typography

Three voices, one hierarchy

Cormorant Garamond

Display · Name & motto

A high-contrast Garamond with sharp, calligraphic detail. Bold for the school name, italic for the motto.

CORMORANT CAPS

Formal · Seal & descriptor

The same family in widely spaced capitals for the seal ring and “Integrated School”: one voice, two registers.

Plus Jakarta Sans

Text · Labels & body

A clear contemporary sans for body copy, labels and small details such as “EST. 2012”.
